Where to Stay in Koh Phangan?

heroSub: 12 hand-picked Koh Phangan hotels across every budget — from Santhiya's teak villas and Anantara's pool villas on Thong Nai Pan Noi beach to yoga and wellness centres around Sri Thanu, down to a design hostel in Thong Sala from ฿450/night. heroStats: 🏝️ 4 key areas (Thong Nai Pan Noi·Sri Thanu·Haad Rin·Thong Sala)
introH2: 🏝️ Why does choosing the right area in Koh Phangan matter so much?
introHtml: Koh Phangan isn't an island where one beach is much like the next — each has its own character, and they're separated by winding, hilly roads. Thong Nai Pan Noi in the north is the luxury resort and pool-villa zone, with gorgeous, quiet beaches and clear water (Santhiya, Anantara, Panviman), but it's about 45 minutes to an hour from Thong Sala pier over steep roads. Sri Thanu in the west is the island's wellness capital — yoga, detox, vegan food and seaside sunsets (Orion, Loyfa). Haad Rin in the south is the home of the Full Moon Party, the first place partygoers look. And Thong Sala is the pier town — the hub for restaurants, the night market, and ferries to and from Samui, ideal for budget travellers and people in transit (Tide & Tribe, The 1, Araya). Many people book a luxury resort up north expecting to nip down to Haad Rin every night, then burn the whole trip driving up and down the hills. This guide rounds up 12 Koh Phangan hotels we've already reviewed across every tier — with real guest-review scores, a 3-site price comparison and direct booking links for each.
mrtHtml: Koh Phangan has no organised public transport; you get around by songthaew (shared taxi truck), private taxi, or rented scooter/car, and many roads are steep and winding — so your choice of area really sets up the trip. Stays around Thong Nai Pan Noi (north) have the prettiest, quietest beaches but sit 45 minutes to an hour from the pier; most resorts run golf-buggy or shuttle services because the terrain is steep. Sri Thanu and Haad Yao (west) are the wellness and sunset zone, with vegan cafés and yoga classes, about a 20–30 minute drive from the pier. Haad Rin (south) is near Haad Rin pier and is the Full Moon Party spot — lively and loud on party nights. Thong Sala is the pier town, within walking distance of restaurants, the night market, and ferries to Samui and Surat Thani — easiest if you don't have a vehicle. The areas in this guide: Thong Nai Pan Noi — luxury resorts, quiet beaches · Sri Thanu–Haad Yao — wellness, yoga, sunsets · Haad Rin — Full Moon Party · Thong Sala — pier, food, budget stays.

entries.addr: 22/2 Moo 5, Thong Nai Pan Noi Beach, Ban Tai, Koh Phangan
entries.storyHtml: Santhiya Koh Phangan is the most-reviewed luxury resort in this guide — 2,135 reviews — and the defining image of high-end Koh Phangan, built almost entirely in carved teak, scoring 8.7. It clings to a hillside above Thong Nai Pan Noi beach in the north. Real guest reviews praise the teak craftsmanship and authentic Thai atmosphere you won't find elsewhere on the island, villas with private pools and sea views that feel good value for this luxury tier, and a quiet private beach made for honeymoons. The trade-off: the steep terrain means relying on shuttle buggies up and down (sometimes with a wait), in-resort dining is pricey, and it's about 30 minutes from the pier — not a party base. Best for couples, honeymooners and anyone here to genuinely switch off.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a villa higher up the hill for the fullest sea view, but be ready for steps or a buggy wait. In-resort food is expensive and heading out isn't easy, so plan your main meals ahead. Book well in advance over high season and Full Moon nights — it fills fast.

Many villas have their own pool. Real guest reviews praise the seclusion and calm, a villa host who replies fast on WhatsApp and looks after you in-room, a clear-water white-sand beach ringed by hills, and a generous fresh breakfast. The catch: it's remote — a winding 45-minute to one-hour drive up from the pier — drink prices are high, and the private-pool water can run cool in spots. Best for couples and higher-budget honeymooners who want a quiet pool villa, full stop.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Message the villa host on WhatsApp ahead about pier transfers — the climb is long and winding. If you want warmer pool water, ask for a villa that gets sun. Drink prices are high, so budget accordingly.

entries.storyHtml: Panviman Resort Koh Phangan is a five-star beachfront resort in the north that delivers hillside sea views at a more reachable price than a pure pool-villa stay, scoring 8.4 from 1,782 reviews (the second-most in this guide). Real guest reviews praise the sweeping sea views — many rooms look right over the bay — a quiet, clear-water private beach with free kayaks and snorkel gear, friendly staff and an on-call golf-buggy shuttle, plus a kids' club and family rooms. The trade-offs: the terrain is very steep, so you're climbing stairs or calling a buggy, some rooms' furnishings show their age, and it's 45 minutes to an hour from the pier. Best for families and couples who want a scenic beachfront resort without top-luxury pricing.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Call for a golf buggy any time if you'd rather not tackle the stairs on the steep grounds. Borrow the free kayaks and snorkel gear and head out in the calm morning water. Travelling as a family, pick a family room and send the kids to the kids' club.

entries.storyHtml: Orion Healing Centre is a genuine wellness centre that nails the yoga-and-detox side of Koh Phangan — a seaside yoga shala on Sri Thanu at an accessible price, scoring 8.6 from 344 reviews. Real guest reviews praise the seaside yoga shala for sunrise and sunset practice, quality yoga teachers and detox programme staff who genuinely care, vegan food so good many forget they're eating clean, and a calm vibe perfect for resetting away from the Full Moon scene. The thing to understand: this is a retreat-style stay — some rooms are starting to age, bookings and admin can occasionally stumble, and it's a vegan, alcohol-free space, not a regular holiday resort. Best for yoga people and anyone here for a serious detox.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Check the class and detox-course schedule ahead, since many guests come specifically for the programmes. Want A/C? Choose Superior or Deluxe — the Bamboo Hut is fan-only. It's alcohol-free and vegan, so come in with retreat expectations before you book.

entries.storyHtml: Tide & Tribe Hostel Phangan is the cheapest stay in this guide, from just ฿450, and it earns a high 8.9 on design and cleanliness right in the middle of Thong Sala, from 40 reviews. It's a newer place in the pier town, within walking distance of the pier, night market and restaurants — handy for anyone in transit to and from Samui. Real guest reviews praise the new, well-designed, very clean rooms, owner Aykut who's friendly and helpful, and a quiet, safe vibe that isn't a party hostel. The trade-offs: it's not on the beach and has no pool (you'll need transport to swim), it's small (12 rooms) and fills fast in high season and on Full Moon nights, it's adults-only, and there's some road noise at night. Best for solo backpackers and budget couples.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: With only 12 rooms it sells out fast on Full Moon nights and in high season — book ahead. It's adults-only, so check before booking if you're travelling as a family. It's not on the beach, so rent a scooter or grab a ride to go swimming.

entries.storyHtml: Loyfa Natural Resort is a Sri Thanu boutique resort whose edge is its private cove and sunset views at a mid-range price, scoring 8.2 from 440 reviews. It sits on Sri Thanu beach in the west, the same zone as the wellness scene and cafés. Real guest reviews praise the bungalows and cottages scattered up the hillside looking out over the Gulf, a private cove that's lovely for sunsets, and a lush, natural setting — with options from simple garden-view rooms up to a Pool Villa with its own pool. Best for couples and anyone wanting a sunset-side resort that isn't as far out as the north coast — it's a 20–30 minute drive from the pier, handier than Thong Nai Pan Noi.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a hillside sea-view cottage for the fullest sunset view. The Sri Thanu side has lots of vegan spots and cafés, so rent a scooter to explore the zone. Book ahead in high season, as the cove-side rooms go fast.

Best for mid-budget travellers who want a pool and a near-pier location without paying resort prices. Entry-level rooms are fairly compact — for more space, go for a Deluxe or Pool Access room.

entries.storyHtml: Phangan Beach Resort is a budget beachfront bungalow stay in Ban Tai that puts you right on the island's longest beach for a few hundred to a thousand baht, scoring 8.3 from 110 reviews. It's on the south coast, between Thong Sala pier and Haad Rin — handy both for trips into town and for popping over to the Full Moon. Real guest reviews praise the beachfront location, garden bungalows in fan and A/C options, and the value for a stay on the sand. Bear in mind it's a budget bungalow place — facilities are simple for the price, the fan rooms suit hardier travellers, and the beach on this side is shallow at low tide. Best for backpackers and budget couples who really want to sleep by the water.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For more comfort, pick an A/C Garden Bungalow or the Deluxe Beach bungalow nearest the sand. The Ban Tai side is shallow at low tide, so check the tide times if you want to swim. It's mid-island, so rent a scooter for easy runs to the pier and Haad Rin.

entries.addr: 94/2 Moo 6, Haad Rin Nai, Koh Phangan
entries.storyHtml: Rin Beach Resort is the best Full Moon Party base in this guide — a beach resort in Haad Rin within walking distance of the pier and the party beach, scoring 7.6 from 670 reviews. It sits on Haad Rin Nai, slightly quieter than the party side. Real guest reviews praise the large resort grounds, a big pool, a shady garden, and over-water sea-view bungalows with big balconies, all at a good price for a beachfront stay in Haad Rin. But to be straight: reviews are polarised — room upkeep and cleanliness are inconsistent, some rooms are aging, water pressure is weak, Wi-Fi drops, and the private beach is shallow with boats moored. Best for Full Moon visitors who want to stay close and care more about location and price than newness.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Staying here on a Full Moon night, you can easily walk back — but book far ahead, as Haad Rin fills fast and rates climb. Reviews are split, so ask to see a room or choose a Superior/Sea View in better shape. The private beach is shallow with boats, better for looking at than swimming — use the pool instead.

entries.storyHtml: Sandy Bay Bungalows is a budget beach bungalow stay at the south end of Haad Yao on the west coast, for anyone who wants to sleep by the sea and catch the sunset for a few hundred baht, scoring 7.0 from 247 reviews. Haad Yao is a clear-water west-coast beach that's good for snorkelling and sunsets. Real guest reviews praise the beachfront location, the raised Hillside bungalows with panoramic bay views, and prices that are very light for a stay on the sand, in fan and A/C options. It is a simple budget bungalow place, though — basic rooms and facilities, it's at the far end of the beach so you'll want a vehicle, and the fan rooms suit hardier travellers. entries.storyHtml: Chaloklum Bay Resort is a beachfront resort on Chaloklum Bay in the north, standing out for its quiet fishing-village atmosphere and a seaside pool, scoring 6.5 from 85 reviews (the lowest in this guide). Chaloklum is a white-sand, clear-water fishing village with a reef close to shore. Real guest reviews praise the beachfront location, a pool facing the sea for sunset watching, free breakfast, Wi-Fi and parking, and the calm where you can walk to seafood in the village. But honestly, per the real reviews: many rooms are old, with damp walls, peeling paint and deferred maintenance, cleanliness and service are inconsistent, and it's far from the pier and main shops, so you need a vehicle. Best for those who want to escape the crowds into a simple fishing village — and are willing to inspect the room first.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Reviews say room condition varies a lot — ask for a Superior Seaview nearer the pool and beach in better shape, and view the room before check-in. Rent a scooter or car since it's far from town. Hit the pool in the evening for the sunset, then walk into the village for seafood.

adviceTitle: How to pick the right Koh Phangan hotel for you

advice.head: Honeymoon / luxury, pool villas
advice.bodyHtml: → Anantara Rasananda ฿11,000, private pool villas, top score 9.2 · or Santhiya ฿4,500, teak villas on a quiet beach, the island icon · easier on the budget, pick Panviman ฿2,800, beachfront with hill views.

advice.head: Wellness, yoga, detox
advice.bodyHtml: → Orion Healing Centre ฿1,500, a yoga-and-detox centre on Sri Thanu beach with vegan food · or stay on the sunset side at Loyfa Natural Resort ฿1,800, private-cove bungalows in the same wellness zone.

advice.head: Full Moon Party, Haad Rin
advice.bodyHtml: → Rin Beach Resort ฿1,000, on Haad Rin Nai, walk to the party beach, big pool · or Phangan Beach Resort ฿900, beach bungalows in Ban Tai, between the pier and Haad Rin.

advice.head: On a budget, best value
advice.bodyHtml: → Tide & Tribe Hostel ฿450, a design hostel scoring 8.9 in central Thong Sala · or The 1 Boutique ฿750, a private A/C room near the pier · or Sandy Bay Bungalows ฿800, beach bungalows on Haad Yao.

advice.head: Sleep by the beach, modest budget
advice.bodyHtml: → Phangan Beach Resort ฿900, bungalows on the island's longest beach · or Sandy Bay Bungalows ฿800, on west-coast Haad Yao with sunsets · or Chaloklum Bay ฿1,500, on Chaloklum Bay with a seaside pool.

advice.head: Stay near the pier / transit to Samui
advice.bodyHtml: → Tide & Tribe Hostel ฿450, walk to the pier, well designed · or The 1 Boutique ฿750, a private room in central Thong Sala · or Araya Boutique ฿900, a boutique with a pool near the pier.

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate from-rates for standard rooms and can change by date and season — always check live prices and compare the 3 sites before booking. On Full Moon Party nights and in high season (Dec–Feb), prices jump sharply and stays around Haad Rin and Thong Sala fill fast, so book several weeks to several months ahead. Almost everything around Thong Nai Pan Noi in the north and Chaloklum Bay is easier with a car/scooter or a resort shuttle, as many roads are steep and winding. Stays in central Thong Sala are easiest if you don't have a vehicle, with the pier to Samui and Surat Thani close by. Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Koh Phangan hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area should I stay in on Koh Phangan?
faq.a: It depends on your style of trip. Thong Nai Pan Noi (north) suits luxury and honeymoon travellers, with quiet beautiful beaches but 45 min–1 hr from the pier (Santhiya, Anantara, Panviman). Sri Thanu–Haad Yao (west) suits wellness, yoga and sunset seekers (Orion, Loyfa, Sandy Bay). Haad Rin (south) suits Full Moon Party-goers (Rin Beach, Phangan Beach). And Thong Sala, the pier town, is within walking distance of restaurants and the night market — easiest if you don't have a vehicle (Tide & Tribe, The 1, Araya).

faq.q: ❓ How much do Koh Phangan hotels cost?
faq.a: Prices vary widely: budget hostels and bungalows start around ฿450–1,000 per night (Tide & Tribe, The 1, Sandy Bay, Phangan Beach, Araya); mid-range resorts and boutiques run about ฿1,000–2,800 (Rin Beach, Orion, Loyfa, Chaloklum, Panviman); and luxury resorts and pool villas run from about ฿4,500–11,000 and up (Santhiya, Anantara). All prices are approximate from-rates for standard rooms, and they're much higher than usual on Full Moon nights and in high season.

faq.q: ❓ Where should I stay for the Full Moon Party?
faq.a: If you want to walk to the party beach, stay in Haad Rin — Rin Beach Resort ฿1,000 on Haad Rin Nai has large grounds, a big pool and walking access to the party beach. To dodge some of the chaos but stay close, choose Phangan Beach Resort ฿900, beach bungalows in Ban Tai between the pier and Haad Rin. On Full Moon nights, Haad Rin stays fill very fast and prices rise, so book several weeks to several months ahead.

faq.q: ❓ Where should I stay for a retreat or yoga on Koh Phangan?
faq.a: Koh Phangan's wellness hub is the Sri Thanu side. Orion Healing Centre ฿1,500 is a genuine yoga-and-detox centre with a seaside yoga shala, vegan food and an alcohol-free setting — ideal if you're here for the programmes. If you'd rather have a quiet resort in the same zone within reach of nearby yoga classes, pick Loyfa Natural Resort ฿1,800, private-cove bungalows on the sunset side.

faq.q: ❓ Can I get around Koh Phangan without a car or scooter?
faq.a: Koh Phangan has no organised public transport, so without a vehicle staying in central Thong Sala is easiest — you can walk to restaurants, the night market and the ferries to Samui (Tide & Tribe, The 1, Araya). The north-coast resorts (Thong Nai Pan Noi, Chaloklum) and Haad Yao are far out with steep roads, so rent a scooter, use the resort shuttle, or charter a songthaew.

faq.q: ❓ Which site is cheapest for booking a Koh Phangan hotel?
faq.a: Prices on each site (Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com) vary with the promotions running at the time, so open all 3 and compare before every booking — each review page in this guide has the price-comparison links. It can save you hundreds to over a thousand baht a night, especially for the northern luxury resorts and Haad Rin stays on Full Moon nights.
